summary.text: Bernadette Gray is the Libertarian candidate for Richmond at the 2026 Victorian election, according to the ABC's guide. The ABC describes her as a nurse whose work has covered neonatal, aged and palliative care, and as a mother of four and grandmother of nine. As at early November 2026 the Libertarians' Victorian election page did not list her, and the ABC gave no website for her.

sources.title: Richmond: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Election 2026, Libertarians Victoria

summary.text: Charles Aponso is the Liberal candidate for Richmond at the 2026 Victorian election. He is studying at university and works in hospitality alongside his studies, and he lives in Melbourne's south-east. His party page focuses on safety and on housing for young people who want to live near the city centre.

priorities.text: More police and tougher consequences for violent offenders, under the Liberals' plan
More homes near the CBD so young Victorians can live closer to the city
Lower living costs

sources.title: Richmond: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Charles Aponso, Liberal for Richmond, Liberal Victoria

summary.text: Chris Dite is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Richmond at the 2026 Victorian election. A teacher, he arrived in the area in 2006 to take up his first teaching job at a local public high school, and for over a decade he also worked night shifts at a local bookshop, where he helped bring in a union between 2017 and 2020. He helped lead the 2013-14 campaign against the East West Link and has been active in campaigns against the sale of public housing and against cuts to cohealth.

prior_roles.role: Union organising at a local bookshop

priorities.text: Stopping the sale of public housing
Protecting local health services from cohealth's cuts
Organising against the far right
Using a seat in Parliament to press the demands of local workers and residents

sources.title: Richmond: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Chris Dite, Victorian Socialists

summary.text: Christine Maynard is standing as an independent for Richmond at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. The ABC's guide links to a Facebook page for the campaign but carries no biography, and no other published profile of them was found as at 9 Nov 2026.

summary.text: David Meyer is standing as an independent for Richmond at the 2026 Victorian election. He runs a business in Richmond and has a background in hospitality; before coming to Australia he spent close to ten years in Japan, moving up from school leadership to principal and then chief executive in international education. He has a master's degree from the Queensland University of Technology in education and leadership, and the ABC says he has also worked with the Queensland government.

priorities.text: More visible police, better street lighting and action on repeat offenders
Less red tape and quicker approvals so safe businesses can open sooner
Bringing empty shopfronts back into use and backing local traders
Keeping Richmond's supervised injecting room open but moving it away from the nearby primary school, homes and businesses by mid-2027
I won't promise powers a State MP doesn't have.

sources.title: Richmond: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
David Meyer, Independent for Richmond
Meet David, David Meyer for Richmond

summary.text: Gabrielle de Vietri has been the Greens MP for Richmond since 2022. She was a Yarra councillor from 2020 and the city's mayor in 2020-21, and worked as a visual artist before that. She chairs the Greens party room and is the party's spokesperson on housing, renters, the arts and other areas. She is recontesting Richmond in 2026.

prior_roles.role: Spokesperson for Public and Affordable Housing

legal_and_integrity.text: Suspended from Parliament for posting a photo on social media of a climate protest inside Parliament.

priorities.text: Renters' rights and public housing
Ending reliance on coal and gas
Integrity in politics
Zero-carbon public transport, walking and cycling
Support for artists and arts workers

sources.title: Gabrielle de Vietri, Parliament of Victoria
Gabrielle de Vietri, Wikipedia

summary.text: Harrison Rindfleish is the One Nation candidate for Richmond at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC's guide says he is studying law and commerce and was raised on the NSW Central Coast. One Nation's page for him refused our requests, so the ABC is the only source here.

sources.title: Richmond: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

priorities.text: Transparent, accountable government and respectful debate
Evidence-based representation and frank discussion of how Victoria raises and spends money
Tackling social isolation and loneliness
Stronger local communities and more community participation

summary.text: Jack Pead-Philipson, who campaigns as Jack Pead, is the Australian Democrats candidate for Richmond at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. The party says his career has been in energy and climate policy, with the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, the International Committee of the Red Cross and private energy companies, and that he lived in the United States from 2016 to 2022. He grew up in Ivanhoe, lives in Abbotsford, and belonged to two other parties before joining the Democrats.

summary.text: Sarah McKenzie is Labor's candidate for Richmond at the 2026 Victorian election. She was elected to Yarra City Council for Yarra Bend Ward in 2024 and served as the council's deputy mayor from late 2024 to late 2025. Before that she was policy director of an independent think tank, and Labor says she grew up in inner Melbourne.

occupation.text: Councillor; formerly a think-tank policy director

priorities.text: Reducing inequality and strengthening local communities
Easing cost-of-living pressure on households, including renters
